name: VUSIS-II
aliases: Value of Urodynamics prior to Stress Incontinence Surgery II
question: In women with stress-predominant incontinence and discordant urodynamic findings, is immediate sling surgery noninferior to treatment tailored to those findings?

design.blinding: Participants and clinicians unblinded; subjective outcome data entry blinded to allocation
design.population: Women with predominant stress urinary incontinence eligible for surgery on clinical assessment whose urodynamic findings were discordant with that assessment; prior incontinence surgery, prolapse at least 1 cm beyond the hymen, and postvoid residual of 150 mL or more were excluded.
design.description: Multicenter diagnostic cohort with embedded noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1000-1001; Figure 1, p 1002

verdictNote: Noninferiority was met; 62/64 and 61/62 assigned women had sling surgery by one year.
takeaway: Among women with discordant urodynamics, immediate sling surgery was noninferior to urodynamics-guided tailored therapy for 12-month Urogenital Distress Inventory urinary-incontinence subscale improvement (44 versus 39 points; mean difference 5, one-sided 95% CI −∞ to 5); almost all women in both arms underwent sling surgery.

reports.label: Primary 12-month report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed list May 2013; exact online date unavailable
reports.citation: van Leijsen SAL, Kluivers KB, Mol BWJ, et al. "Value of Urodynamics Before Stress Urinary Incontinence Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2013;121(5):999-1008. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e31828c68e3
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, p 1001; Table 4, p 1005

results.endpoint: Urogenital Distress Inventory urinary-incontinence subscale improvement
results.measure: Mean 12-month improvement in randomized patients with valid observations (115/126); points; mean difference (immediate surgery minus tailored therapy)
results.note: Intention-to-treat analysis based on valid observations. The reported one-sided 95% confidence interval for the mean difference was −∞ to 5 points; the prespecified noninferiority margin was 5 points. No primary-endpoint P value was reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1001; Figure 1, p 1002; Results and Table 4, pp 1004-1005

results.endpoint: Subjective cure of stress urinary incontinence
results.measure: No activity-related leakage on Urogenital Distress Inventory at 12 months; randomized patients with valid observations
results.note: Subjective cure required a negative response to the activity-related leakage item; any leakage counted as failure.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1001; Results and Table 4, pp 1004-1005

results.endpoint: Objective cure of stress urinary incontinence
results.measure: Negative stress test at 12 months; randomized patients tested
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1001; Results and Table 4, pp 1004-1005

results.measure: Improved at 12 months on seven-point scale; randomized patients with valid observations
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1001; Table 4, p 1005

harms.label: Reoperation
harms.note: The observational cohort had 13/452 reoperations. Across all 14 reoperations, indications were tape exposure (n=3), large residual urine (n=7), or persistent or recurrent stress incontinence (n=4).

harms.label: Prolonged catheterization and early sling release
harms.note: Clean intermittent catheterization for longer than six weeks was indicated in 8/453 (2%) operated women; five underwent sling release in the first postoperative days. Two further reoperations were indicated for large postvoid residuals.

harms.label: Tape exposure requiring reoperation
harms.note: Three women in the 452-person observational cohort underwent reoperation for tape exposure.

delivery.label: Diagnostic cohort and randomization
delivery.value: Of 602 women who underwent urodynamics, 578 were eligible and enrolled; 268/578 (46%) had findings discordant with clinical assessment, and 126/268 consented to randomization (64 immediate surgery, 62 tailored therapy). Primary outcome data were complete for 115/126 (91%).
delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 1, p 1002; Results, pp 1002-1003

delivery.label: Assigned treatment strategies
delivery.value: Women with discordant findings were assigned either immediate midurethral sling surgery or individually tailored therapy based on urodynamics; tailored options included sling surgery, anticholinergics, pelvic floor exercises or bladder training, pessary, expectant management, intravesical botulinum toxin, or pretibial nerve stimulation.

delivery.label: Sling uptake and routes by one year
delivery.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Results, p 1004
delivery.note: Initial surgery occurred in 61/64 (95%) and 57/62 (92%), respectively; one immediate-surgery participant received drug treatment based on detrusor overactivity after the operation was postponed.

reports.label: Retrospective sling cohort follow-up
reports.citation: Mengerink BB, Pluymen EE, van Leijsen SAL, et al. "Persistent or Recurrent Urinary Incontinence 8 Years After Midurethral Sling Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study." *Int Urogynecol J.* 2025;36(12):2401-2410. doi:10.1007/s00192-025-06183-1
reports.followUp: Median 7.8 years from surgery to chart review; median 2 months from surgery to last recorded clinical visit
reports.followUpLocator: PDF p2404, Results, paragraph before Postoperative UI

results.endpoint: Postoperative urinary incontinence recorded in charts
results.measure: Pooled operated cohort, retrospective file review; no randomized-arm comparison
results.note: Symptoms were recorded in 71/301 (23.6%): SUI in 38/301 (12.6%), including persistent SUI in 18/301 (6.0%) and recurrent SUI in 20/301 (6.6%); urgency incontinence in 51/301 (16.9%), including 18 with mixed symptoms.
results.locator: PDF pp2401,2404, Abstract and Postoperative UI; Figure 1

results.measure: Pooled operated cohort, treatment documented among women with incontinence
results.note: Additional treatment was documented in 42/71 (59.2%) women with incontinence; repeat sling placement in 5/301 (1.7%) of the overall reviewed cohort.
results.locator: PDF p2406, Additional Treatment; p2407, Discussion

harms.label: Tape exposure and obstructive voiding
harms.locator: PDF p2406, Postoperative UI and Other Complaints
harms.note: Tape exposure was documented in 7/301 (2.3%); obstructive voiding symptoms, including retention, in 22/301 (7.3%).

harms.label: Sling revision
harms.locator: PDF pp2406-2407, Additional Treatment and Discussion
harms.note: Five tape-exposure excisions and nine tape transections were documented; the discussion reports 17 sling-related repeat surgeries overall, including five repeat sling placements.

delivery.label: Definition of discordance in the original cohort
delivery.value: Discordance included absent demonstrable stress leakage, detrusor overactivity, weak bladder contractility or flow, elevated residual, outflow obstruction, or abnormal cystometric capacity, sensation, or compliance.

delivery.label: Operative routes in the reviewed cohort
delivery.value: The original trial allowed retropubic or transobturator midurethral slings at surgeon discretion and excluded single-incision slings; the reviewed cohort contained 88 retropubic and 213 transobturator procedures.
delivery.locator: PDF pp2402-2403, Materials and Methods and Results; Table 1

delivery.label: Records available for retrospective review
delivery.value: Of 506 original participants who initially underwent sling surgery, 301 charts from 12/30 original hospitals were analyzed after 44 records with insufficient or absent follow-up were excluded.
delivery.locator: PDF pp2402-2403, Materials and Methods and Results
